recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft in giant mechanical arms for the first time Saturday, clearing another obstacle en route to Elon Musk’s vision of making crewed space launches as routine as air travel. recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: A single faulty router may have triggered the nationwide ground stop ordered by the Federal Aviation Administration on Friday, underscoring the dangers posed by the US’ outmoded technological infrastructure. recent_candidates.author: Ben Smith
recent_candidates.excerpt: The Scene A year before the iconic show debuted on HBO in April of 2014, the writer Alec Berg met the show’s creator, Mike Judge, in an anonymous Santa Monica office. Judge was wrestling with the pilot for a show about Silicon Valley’s power and its eccentricity, but it wasn’t working and he wanted a second opinion. Berg thought he saw part of the problem. There was a scene in the pilot where Richard Hendricks, the protagonist and founder of the company Pied Piper, is trying to buy a car he can’t afford. Berg told Judge the scene didn’t make sense: “This is not a guy who’s materialistic,” he said. “He’s an artist.” Berg took over the writer’s room and would eventually become showrunner of the comedy, which ran for six seasons and helped shape the culture it depicted, parodied, and at times glorified. We reached him in Los Angeles Thursday to ask him how he and Judge and their cast had nailed the Silicon Valley scene of the mid-2010s app boom — and, above all, why the show remains uncannily relevant today, from its depiction of tortured founders and unreflective investors to the uncanny conclusion in which the Pied Piper crew builds an AI model too powerful to release. Their moment of realization comes when their AI, Son of Anton, let loose on Pied Piper’s code, concludes that the most efficient way to eliminate bugs is to delete the software. recent_candidates.excerpt: Foreign Affairs What Trump Can Get Out of the Trilateral Shenzhen Summit There are several files on which three great powers can make tangible progress at the upcoming meeting. But whether the aspiration for a more peaceful and stable global order can be met during the Shenzhen meeting expected this month is open to question. Doubts are visible in all corners. Still, it would be a mistake to pass up such an extraordinary opportunity. I have written in a recent book that this brand of trilateralism is necessary to knit a dysfunctional global order back together. In particular, this three-way meeting has the possibility to make progress on both nuclear stability and regional conflict, issues that are haunting our world at present with the specter of uncontrolled, violent escalation to even more tragic levels. Trilateral diplomacy presents unique challenges, but such a summit contains the potential of breaking free from the assumptions that too often stall bilateral or multilateral agreements. Daniel Byman Efforts to span the divide between international affairs scholars and policymakers have made progress in recent years. A host of initiatives, from broad fora like Bridging the Gap to specialized offerings like those from the Project on Nuclear Issues , have been introduced. These programs perform valuable functions, training scholars on skills like briefing, drafting op-eds, and selecting policy-relevant research questions. They also cultivate relationships among scholars, practitioners, and those straddling both worlds. But as graduates of policy-oriented Ph.D. programs who have pursued varied careers in U.S. foreign and defense policy, we still see missing planks in the bridge connecting scholars and policymakers. recent_candidates.excerpt: Israel's data shows it allowed half of the promised aid trucks into Gaza Israel has failed to meet its commitments under the Gaza ceasefire deal, allowing in only around half the agreed volume of humanitarian and commercial goods each month since March, Israeli military data shows. Data obtained by Haaretz newspaper showed a growing shortfall in food deliveries to Gaza, alongside severe shortages of medical supplies, tents and materials to repair damaged infrastructure. Torrential rains have flooded displacement camps, leaving hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in increasingly dire conditions. Under the ceasefire deal, Israel pledged to allow 4,200 vehicles carrying humanitarian and commercial goods into Gaza each week, equivalent to roughly 18,200 a month. Deliveries were to include food, fuel, medical supplies and equipment, shelter materials and equipment to repair essential infrastructure. Data supplied by the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (Cogat) to the US-led International Gaza Support Center (IGSC) show that Israel allowed about 4,700 trucks into Gaza in March, rising to 5,300 in April and more than 9,600 in May. It comes after MEE uncovered details of a previously unreported 158m-shekel ($49.8m) contract between Toyota and Israel’s Ministry of Defense for the supply of forklifts that was signed in 2024 – the first full year of the Gaza war . Toyota says that its vehicles are not intended for military use. When asked about the contract, the company told MEE it had commitments in place with both the defence ministry and its official reseller in Israel to ensure that its technology and products were “for civil use only”. But when MEE then shared footage posted on official Israeli military social media channels, which showed Toyota forklifts being used at locations including a missiles and ammunition depot in northern Israel, a Logistics Corps training base, and inside a munitions factory, it said it was investigating the images to determine whether those agreements had been breached. recent_candidates.title: What men’s magazines did to sex
recent_candidates.author: Terri White
recent_candidates.excerpt: It wasn’t so much the straw that broke the camel’s back as the rope. Rough manila rope to be specific: about an inch and a half in diameter, looped around my neck. It was 2016, and my cool-ass liberal views on pornography and sex were shaky at best, the night my boyfriend picked up the ends and pulled hard. My airway cut off, black bled into my peripheral vision. He pulled again, harder. Tiny white stars burst in the darkness, a throbbing drum beat filling my ears as blood bound for my brain stopped dead. As I gasped — well, tried to — in blind-panic and mock-excitement, I couldn’t help but wonder… was this empowerment ? Was this where a decade and half of choice feminism had got me? And, well, it’s precisely where. Saying “yes” as he strangled me so hard that spiral-groove abrasions crawled down my throat afterwards. But then, this night on my back and entirely in his hand scared me sane, was the hinge of my sexual politics. A decade prior, in 2006, I was a committed choice feminist (we should support any-and-all choices a woman makes, including those for the pleasure and profit of men), and a senior editor on men’s weekly magazine Nuts (see previous brackets). A decade on, in 2026, I’m an anti-porn radical feminist, surveying where two-plus decades of choice feminism — and its rabid little sister, pick-me feminism (we should support any-and-all choices a woman makes, unless it obstructs the pleasure and profit of men) — has got us as a society. Sánchez a Lula: «Cuando la izquierda cree en la victoria, frente a los análisis adversos, al final, si la izquierda cree en la victoria, la acaba logrando». pic.twitter.com/UoAUxP46ST — THE OBJECTIVE (@TheObjective_es) November 16, 2026 «Es muy importante, Pedro, que tú ganes las elecciones en España», ha declarado Lula en una conversación con Sánchez, según ha informado este lunes el PSOE en un comunicado. El mandatario brasileño ha reivindicado a Sánchez como «la persona indicada» para «seguir defendiendo la democracia en Europa» y para ayudar «a defenderla en América Latina». Por su parte, Sánchez ha destacado «la remontada épica» de Lula en Brasil, que ganó la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales brasileñas el pasado 25 de octubre , superando por la mínima al candidato ultraderechista Flávio Bolsonaro , quien había sido vencedor en la primera ronda. Sánchez recluta al gurú electoral de Lula en plena campaña del 29-N Manu Torralba «Me lleva siempre a la misma conclusión y es que, pese a las encuestas y los análisis adversos que se puedan hacer, al final, si la izquierda cree en la victoria, acaba logrando esa victoria. Y tú lo lograste»

recent_candidates.title: La Unión Europea en el Ártico: una estrategia para la vecindad septentrional
recent_candidates.author: Javier Ivars Pérez, Mira Milosevich-Juaristi.
recent_candidates.excerpt: Mensajes clave La nueva Estrategia europea para el Ártico (2026) supone un nuevo paso en la evolución de la aproximación de la Unión Europea (UE) a la región. Esta ha pasado de una política centrada en el medio ambiente, el desarrollo sostenible y la cooperación multilateral, con Rusia como “socio estratégico”, a otra en la que la seguridad, la autonomía estratégica y la defensa de los intereses europeos ocupan un lugar central. Este giro responde a la confluencia del acelerado calentamiento de la región, el deterioro de las relaciones con Rusia tras la invasión de Ucrania y la creciente proyección de China, a lo que se suman las tensiones transatlánticas. La estrategia asume que el multilateralismo, aunque indispensable, ya no puede ser el único fundamento de la aproximación europea. La UE aspira a ser una “potencia geopolítica” en el Ártico, pero su naturaleza no estatal restringe esa ambición. Una política exterior intergubernamental, capacidades militares fragmentadas y una dependencia estructural de Estados Unidos (EEUU) y de la Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte (OTAN) limitan a la UE actuar como un actor estratégico. La principal novedad política de la nueva estrategia es el marco de Vecindad Septentrional. La región pasa así de ser un espacio de competición en el que la UE cuenta con intereses estratégicos a ser considerada parte de su entorno estratégico, sobre cuya configuración política, económica y de seguridad aspira a influir.
